## Lag

`node docfix.Lag (U)` · leaf · [source](../../../tests/doc/lib/docfix/Lag.se)

Follows its input through a first-order lag.

    d/dt y = (vin - y) / tau

The output approaches a constant input exponentially, reaching 63 % of a
step after `tau` ([§6.4](../../../SPECIFICATION.md#64-states)).

### Unit parameters

| Name | Description |
|---|---|
| `U` | unit of the signal |

### Settings

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tau` | `double(s)` | `0.5` | time constant |
| `gain` | `double(-)` | *required* | scale applied to the output |

### Inputs

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `vin` | `double(U)` | signal to follow |

### Outputs

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `vout` | `double(U)` | lagged signal, scaled by `gain` |

### States

| Name | Kind | Type | Initial | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `y` | continuous | `double(U)` | `0.0` | lagged signal before scaling |

**Direct feedthrough:** none; `output()` reads no inputs.

### Initial conditions

`y` starts at zero unless overridden.

### Limitations

`tau` must be positive; zero divides by zero.

### See also

`Pair`, for a record this node does not use.

### Examples

From the node's `tests` section, with `U = m`. Each row is one evaluation; the last column names the case.

**the output is the state times the gain** (exactly)

| `param.gain` | `state.y` | → `out.vout` | Case |
|---|---|---|---|
| `2` | `3` | `6` | doubles |
| `0` | `3` | `0` | zero gain |

**the state moves toward the input** (to within `1e-12`)

| `param.tau` | `state.y` | `in.vin` | → `der.y` | Case |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `0.5` | `0` | `1` | `2` | a unit step at rest |

## Pair

`type docfix.Pair (U)` · record · [source](../../../tests/doc/lib/docfix/Pair.se)

A pair of values sharing one unit.

### Unit parameters

| Name | Description |
|---|---|
| `U` | unit of both elements |

### Fields

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `a` | `double(U)` | first element |
| `b` | `double(U)` | second element |

### Conventions

`a` is the first element and `b` the second.
